subject: OpsLyft hosted API traffic profile and $/1M target
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@opslyft.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + numbers we need to price hosted API

Hi Asha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the few remaining asks so we can put together a firm hosted price and a short-term trial plan.

Recap (from my notes):
- OpsLyft is planning to use hosted API for user-facing summarization + a small classification pipeline.
- Typical request is prompt + model response (we estimated ~400–600 tokens per interaction on the call).
- You expect steady-state traffic with periodic marketing-driven spikes.

What we need to finalize price scenarios: (one-line answers OK)
1) Expected monthly token volume (range or point estimate; e.g. 50M–120M tokens/month).
2) Peak TPS (requests per second) at the application edge during a spike and how long spikes typically last (seconds/minutes).
3) Approx % of traffic that's chat-style back-and-forth vs one-shot generation vs embeddings (if any).
4) Any hard budget target for $/1M tokens you need us to hit for this FY.

Ballpark from Redwood for hosted (will formalize once we have exact volume & commit):
- List hosted band (no commit): ~ $14–16 per 1M tokens
- 12-month committed pricing: typically ~ 15–25% discount relative to list (dependent on volume & SLA)

I'll prepare three scenarios (no-commit, 6-month trial commitment, 12-month commit) once you confirm the numbers above. Attaching a one-page scenario template for quick inline numbers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0196

Attachment: redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Asha Verma <asha@opslyft.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we need to price hosted API

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear list. Answers below, with a couple of notes:

1) Monthly token volume: we are targeting 95M–120M tokens/month in the first 3 months after launch, with a goal of 200M+ by Q3 2028 if engagement scales.

2) Peak TPS: our normal steady-state TPS is ~60–80 rps. We see marketing-driven spikes that push to ~220 rps for up to 30–45 seconds, and rare product events that have pushed to ~400 rps for <60s in our staging load tests. We expect spikes to be short (tens of seconds) but high frequency during launches.

3) Traffic breakdown: ~70% one-shot generation (single prompt -> response), ~25% short chat sessions (2–4 turns), ~5% embeddings (batch jobs at off-peak hours).

4) Budget target: for FY28 leadership prefers an effective target of ~$11 per 1M tokens (they understand discounts come with commits). If we can get a 12-month commit that hits <$11, that'd be attractive.

I've attached our internal estimate CSV that shows our session assumptions and token-per-request samples. Happy to jump on a quick call if anything is unclear.

Cheers,
Asha Verma
Head of Product | OpsLyft
asha@opslyft.ai
+1 (212) 555-0772

Attachment: opslyft_token_estimate.csv (CSV stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@opslyft.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we need to price hosted API

Asha — perfect, this is exactly the level we need. A couple of quick follow-ups so the scenarios are representative:

- When you say "marketing-driven spikes" (220 rps for 30–45s), what's the frequency? (e.g., once/day, a few times/week, a few times/month). This affects how much burst capacity we recommend and whether caching will materially reduce billable tokens.
- For the rare 400 rps spikes, are those synthetic/staging tests or observed in production? If production, did they correspond to increased token size, or mostly concurrent smaller requests?
- For chat sessions: is the average total tokens per session closer to 700–900 (multiple turns) or ~1k+? Helps decide whether to recommend KV caching to reduce repeated prefix costs.

Ballpark commercial note (purely illustrative; formal quote to follow):
- No-commit hosted: $15.50 / 1M tokens (standard band; includes standard routing & 30-day retention)
- 12-mo commit target (100M+/mo): $11.00–12.25 / 1M tokens depending on SLA and burst guarantees

I'll drop an updated scenario spreadsheet with 3 rows: (A) No-commit estimate, (B) 3–6 month trial with burst protection add-on, (C) 12-month commit with preferred pricing + 99.9% tiered SLA. Also including a short note on caching/batching impacts and a recommended peak TPS safety margin.

Attaching the scenario workbook and a copy of our standard hosted SLA for your procurement team.

Thanks — I'll aim to get that over by tomorrow EOD PST.

—Karthik

Attachments: redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx, redwood_sla_v1.pdf

From: Mike Chen <mike@opslyft.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Verma <asha@opslyft.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers we need to price hosted API

Karthik / Asha — quick note from procurement: leadership is comfortable moving forward with a 12-month commitment if we can land at ~$11 / 1M tokens and also get a burst cushion (ability to absorb short spikes up to 400 rps without manual escalation).

We can commit to an initial contract target of 100M tokens/month (with a north-south tolerance of ±20% for the first quarter). Spikes: target is 220 rps typical, with occasional 400 rps bursts for up to 45s — those should be covered by the burst cushion.

Next asks from OpsLyft:
- Please provide a formal quotation with tiered pricing & a short trial addendum (3 weeks pilot)
- Include a note on data retention/audit options (we need 90-day logs, SOC2 controls)
- Send over the DOCuSign/contract draft so procurement can review SLA clauses

If you can get the quote + contract draft by EOD Monday PST that would keep us on track for a Jan 15 internal sign-off.

Thanks — Mike
Procurement Manager | OpsLyft
+1 (415) 555-0344
